extraction.name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset for object detection and segmentation
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár
extraction.citeAs: Lin et al. (2014). Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context. ECCV.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The Microsoft Common Objects in COntext (MS COCO) dataset was collected using a novel pipeline for gathering data with extensive use of Amazon Mechanical Turk. The dataset contains 91 common object categories with 82 of them having more than 5,000 labeled instances.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset was collected from Flickr and other image sources using a technique that queries for pairs of objects in conjunction with images retrieved via scene-based queries.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The annotation pipeline is split into 3 primary tasks: (a) labeling the categories present in the image, (b) locating and marking all instances of the labeled categories, and (c) segmenting each object instance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation pipeline uses a hierarchical labeling approach. Workers on Amazon's Mechanical Turk (AMT) were used to label images. The pipeline consists of category labeling, instance spotting, and instance segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The quality of annotations was analyzed by comparing crowd worker quality on the category labeling task to dedicated expert workers.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image was labeled by 8 workers for a total of ~10k worker hours.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is split into two roughly equal parts. The first half was released in 2014, and the second half will be released in 2015.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to advance the state-of-the-art in object recognition by placing the question of object recognition in the context of the broader question of scene understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset strives to collect images rich in contextual information.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has limitations in terms of data generalization limits and quality issues.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for object detection, segmentation, and scene understanding tasks.
